items.title: Interval-scoped backward Bakry–Émery contraction

source.attribution: Mathlib supplies monotonicity from a nonnegative derivative; Samplinglib applies it to the exact exponential weight used by backward Bakry–Émery interpolation.

items.statement: If Φ has derivative Φ' on [s,t] and Φ'(u)≥rΦ(u) for s<u<t, then Φ(s)≤Φ(t)exp(-r(t-s)).
assumptions: The supplied derivative is a genuine HasDerivAt statement at every point of the closed interval.
The growth inequality is required only in the open interval.
No sign condition on the interpolation or rate is required, and a degenerate interval is allowed.

obligations.label: Convert interval-local derivative growth into the exact backward endpoint factor

bindings.boundary: Concrete semigroup construction, the interpolation derivative identity, the Γ₂ curvature estimate, and terminal-energy identification remain separate prerequisites.

assumption_deltas.source: The standard proof assumes differentiability on the interpolation interval and a derivative lower bound in its interior.
assumption_deltas.lean: Lean exposes genuine HasDerivAt witnesses on the closed interval and the growth bound only on its open interior.
assumption_deltas.reason: The Lean statement exposes the closed-interval derivative witnesses and open-interval growth hypothesis exactly; endpoint derivatives supply the continuity needed by the monotonicity theorem without extending the differential inequality.
